oe_policy.OE-1: Open enrollment runs November 3-21. Elections not submitted by 11:59 pm on November 21 default to the prior year's elections, except that Health FSA and HSA elections reset to zero.
oe_policy.OE-2: Late elections are accepted only if (a) a documented system outage prevented the employee from submitting during the final 48 hours of the window, and (b) the employee submits form OE-L within 5 business days after the outage is resolved.
oe_policy.OE-3: Travel, illness, or not reading open enrollment emails are not grounds for a late election.
oe_policy.OE-4: An approved late election is effective January 1, like any other open enrollment election.
oe_policy.OE-5: The Benefits Committee decides OE-L requests; analysts prepare a recommendation.

leave_codes.FML-C: Family/medical leave, continuous: job protection for a serious health condition
leave_codes.STD: Short-term disability: income replacement for the employee's own non-work illness or injury after a 7-day waiting period, insurer-approved
leave_codes.WC: Workers' compensation: income replacement and medical costs for a work-related injury, claim filed with the carrier
leave_codes.SICK: Sick time, up to 5 consecutive days

wc_policy.WC-1: Work-related injuries must be reported to a supervisor immediately and a first report of injury (FROI) filed within 24 hours by the supervisor.
wc_policy.WC-2: A late report does not bar a claim; HR files the FROI as soon as it learns of the injury and the carrier decides compensability.
wc_policy.WC-3: When a condition has both work and non-work causes, the carrier determines compensability; STD may pay pending that decision.
wc_policy.WC-4: Leads and supervisors who fail to file a FROI after being told of an injury are subject to retraining.

levy_procedure.L-1: A state tax levy is processed when it bears the agency's seal or signature and the taxpayer name and taxpayer identifier match payroll records.
levy_procedure.L-2: The employee's copy and exemption statement form must be delivered to the employee. If the employee copy is missing from the envelope, request it from the agency; withholding still begins using the standard exemption.
levy_procedure.L-3: Child support orders always take priority over tax levies.
levy_procedure.L-4: If the taxpayer identifier does not match payroll records, do not withhold. Call the agency's employer line to verify the identifier before returning the levy.
levy_procedure.L-5: Employee requests to pay the agency directly do not stop a levy; only a written release from the agency does.
levy_procedure.L-6: Levies are logged in the Garnishment Tracker the day they are received, whatever their status.

bulletin_1.text: The Local 12 agreement was ratified on 8/27. The 3.5% general wage increase is retroactive to July 1 for all bargaining-unit classifications. Retro payments will be issued on the 9/30 check. Shift premiums also rise by $0.25/hour from the first full pay period after ratification. Questions: laborrelations@example.com.

Claim line: Temporary housing, Aug 3-Aug 31, Aspen Suites Boise, itemized folio attached, paid by employee, reimbursement requested.

Payroll earning codes for relocation (excerpt from Payroll Coding Guide, rev. 2026-02):
- RLS: Relocation lump-sum allowance paid in cash (taxable wages)
- RDB: Moving company direct-billed to the company (non-cash, taxable, imputed)
- RTH: Temporary housing reimbursed to the employee (taxable wages)
- RHT: Home-sale assistance (taxable)
- RGU: Tax gross-up on relocation items (taxable)
- EXP-NT: Non-taxable business expense reimbursement (travel on company business only; not relocation)
- REG: Regular earnings
- BON: Bonus
- COM: Commission
Note: relocation items are never coded EXP-NT, even when receipts are provided.
